newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong Electric up on switched buying.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Electric up on switched buying.

text.p: Shares of Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd benefited from switched buying in the morning session on Friday, bucking the negative trend in the market, brokers said.
Hongkong Electric, the only blue chip to post a gain in the morning, was up HK$0.30 to HK$27.20. The Hang Seng Index was off 220 points, or 1.7 percent, at 12,697 at the midday break.
"Some say the stock has bottomed out and that utilities are seen as a safe haven for the time being," a broker said.

Brokers said some institutions were seen switching buying to Hongkong Electric from property stocks as market sentiment was dampened by fears of a U.S. interest rate rise and a possible downturn in the overheated local property market.
On Thursday, Hongkong Electric reported 1996 net profit of HK$4.15 billion, a fall of 0.8 percent from the year before.
"The result is largely in line with expectations and the counter is relatively cheap when compared with other utilities," one broker said.
